title: Keel's allocation positions are addressed chain-then-protocol-then-asset, and most of them hold rival stablecoins
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.1.2.1 organizes Keel's Active Allocation System Instances in a three-level directory: network (Solana), then protocol (Kamino, Drift), then asset. Kamino carries five Instances — USDS, USDC, USDT, USDG, PYUSD — and Drift four.

The asset list is the notable part. Keel's mandate is to expand USDS, yet four of every five allocation Instances hold stablecoins Sky does not issue. Deploying into USDC, USDT, USDG and PYUSD positions is how the Agent "generates excess returns on assets in Sky's collateral portfolio": earning yield requires going where the yield is, which on a lending venue means supplying whatever asset the market pays for.

The triple-keyed addressing is what keeps that manageable. Because risk attaches jointly to a chain, a venue and an asset — a Kamino USDT position and a Drift USDT position fail for different reasons — making each combination its own Instance lets any one of them be suspended, re-parameterized or retired without touching the others.

The cost is proliferation: nine Instances for two venues on one chain, each carrying the full Instance skeleton, and each requiring its own governance action to create.
description: The Keel Liquidity Layer runs one Allocation System Instance per (Solana, venue, token) triple — Kamino and Drift across USDS, USDC, USDT, USDG and PYUSD.
